editorial:
Ever wonder who actually started the fight against the Nazi codes? You get to follow three brilliant Polish mathematicians who are way ahead of their time. Instead of just using pencils and paper, these guys build actual replicas of the Enigma machines to figure out how they work. The vibe is a mix of a race against time and a secret spy mission. You feel the pressure as they try to get their hard work to the British and French before the bombs start falling in 1939. It is a great look at the unsung heroes who did the heavy lifting before the war even fully began.

What really works here is how it keeps you interested even though it is mostly about math. The acting feels real, and the tension builds up perfectly as the invasion looms. One downside is that it moves a bit slow in the middle, but the payoff is worth it. If you love history or secrets, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with the Polish team escaping to Algeria and France to keep their work going. They successfully handed over the machines and the secrets to the Allies, which changed the course of the war. However, the sad part is that their huge contribution was mostly ignored by history for a long time. The ending shows them continuing to fight in the shadows, hoping that one day the world will know they were first.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about secret wars and geniuses.
